summary: A 1955 L-4 cab on a 50-foot tower on Conrad Peak. Not staffed since 1984, drive-up, in disrepair; restoration status unclear.

facts.design: L-4 hip-roof cab with catwalk on a 50-foot treated timber tower; replaced a log cupola
facts.status_note: Not staffed since 1984, in disrepair, and no longer used for fire detection.

access.note: Drive-up site on National Forest land. No closure found in the sources. Climbing rules are not documented; ask the St. Joe Ranger District before climbing.

corrections.proposed: 1955 built (current L-4 tower). The earlier log cupola is dated 1924 or 1931 by different sources.
corrections.why: The 1924 date belongs to the log cupola that stood first. The standing tower and its L-4 cab date to 1955.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and Rex's page date the first log cabin to 1924. The register says the cupola it replaced was built in 1931. The story reports both.
The register and firelookout.com give 50 ft. Rex's page gives 53 ft. The record uses 50 ft (15.2 m).
Firelookout.com says restoration work has been ongoing. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it was only proposed, with no work seen as of summer 2020. The story leaves the current status open.
The register gives 6,338 ft (1,932 m). Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 6441 ft. The brief's 1931.8 m comes from the register. Elevation is not in the facts block.
The register says Idaho Panhandle National Forest. Firelookout.com says St. Joe National Forest. The two names cover the same St. Joe area.

notes_for_editor: The cupola date (1924 vs 1931) and tower height (50 vs 53 ft) conflict across sources. The brief's 1924 built event refers to the cupola and is corrected to 1955 for the standing tower. Restoration status is unverified since the 2020 reporting. Check on site before any public claim that restoration is under way.
